Glossop 2010 quote verbatim (abstract); opening untested.

Stocks 2014; opening untested.

entries.note: Nielsen 2012 is a pooled K-PD simulation; NCT00808288 (trough FEV1 primary) never posted results. The entry's quote describes model fit, not a primary result. No admissible primary-endpoint comparison: untested.
entries.adjudication_note: RULE QUESTION: does a model-based meta-analysis (Nielsen 2012 K-PD, 690 patients; simulated trough-FEV1 probabilities) count as the trial's primary endpoint responding under decision 4 when NCT00808288 never reported? Tier 4 admits meta-analyses but the result is simulated.

Breo label in bundle; quote verbatim (label txt line 762) with 7.8 and 17.1 bpm. Predicted on-target tachycardia seen dose-dependently in humans: same. Anoro MedR 10.5/22.3 bpm figures not found by grep.
Aparici 2012; opening untested with stated dog margin 5.6.
Timmer 2014 quote verbatim (abstract). Direction match holds; note the draft's 'above 0.625-10 ug' is loose, since 5 and 10 ug were both effective and palpitation-bearing doses.

Decision 12 transfers safety with imported_from.

entries.note: Glossop 2010 quote verbatim (abstract). Opening untested; whether a PK design rationale is a 'model prediction' is a rule question.
Br J Clin Pharmacol 2013 (PMID 23323609, PMC3853534) resolves; quote verbatim (abstract only). Low heart-rate effect to 280 ug matches the stated design claim; same holds if entry 7's claim counts.

Respir Med 2016 (PMID 27109822, epub 2016-04-01) resolves; quote verbatim (abstract only). Opening untested at 2016; no earlier public ADRB2 analysis for vilanterol (Anoro ClinPharmR 4.2 is CYP2D6/UMEC only).

entries.rule: status table: contra = the model's own prediction failed; 'Also' #58: null-null is same only when the model made the null a prediction; decision 10 not triggered (patient-level answer unknown)
entries.note: Quote verbatim (abstract only). Contra holds: variants chosen for 'prior evidence of associations' predicted differential response; 1795 VI / 6075 patients on primary trough FEV1 is a discriminating null. Not same (null never predicted, #58); not retro (ROCK precedent).

CPT PSP (PMC5869554) resolves to Hendrickx et al., epub 2017-12-27, print March 2018; quote verbatim in Introduction. AZD3199 in Tables 1-2 confirmed (guinea-pig lung IC50 895 nM). Opening untested at 2017.

Quote verbatim in abstract. Supplement Table S5 rows verified: AZD3199 200/400/800 ug od, day 28, 24 h, 99/110/97 mL, 367/734/1468 nM, ratios 0.41/0.82/1.6, citing Kuna 2013 (2013-06-03), so retro under decision 10, never same. No S5 row names PF-00610355; Nielsen 2012 is cited for salmeterol rows.

missing: Condreay et al. 2016, Respir Med, doi:10.1016/j.rmed.2016.03.019 (PMID 27109822): ADRB2 Arg16Gly/Gln27Glu/Thr164Ile pharmacogenetics of vilanterol 25 ug trough-FEV1 response in 17 COPD trials (N=6075, 1795 on VI): no association. A human_genetic, prediction_level patient track for a member drug with no track in the draft.

Boger & Friden 2018, CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol, doi:10.1002/psp4.12270 (PMC5869554, online 2017-12-27): translational lung-PK model for 12 inhaled drugs including AZD3199 (and the PF-00610355 FEV1 data of Nielsen 2012), predicting human lung concentrations that correlate with published COPD trough FEV1. An in_silico retrodiction (retro) track with no entry.

Aparici et al. 2016, Eur J Pharmacol, doi:10.1016/j.ejphar.2015.11.053 (PMID 26656755): dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety index for vilanterol 2.4 (abediterol 10.5, olodaterol 4.9) and guinea-pig bronchoprotective t1/2 18 h for vilanterol, run after vilanterol's approval. A member drug's own model, retrodiction on the dog track; not used by the draft.

Bjermer et al. 2013, Ther Adv Respir Dis, doi:10.1177/1753465813497527 (PMID 23907810; NCT00736489 results posted 2014-04-03): AZD3199 systemic effects (potassium, heart rate, QTc) versus formoterol in asthma; the patient side of the Stocks 2014 guinea-pig potassium comparison (safety 6).

Program stops the draft calls unexplained: abediterol discontinued at Phase II in AstraZeneca's February 2021 pipeline (AdisInsight 800026746) and NCT04199598 terminated 2020 'business prioritizations ... not due to safety concerns' (tier 3 registry record); PF-00610355 stopped 2011 for strategic reasons (Wikipedia only, no admissible source found); AZD3199: no source found. None is a model failure, but the registry termination reason should be cited.

Hughes et al. 2015, Drug Des Devel Ther, doi:10.2147/dddt.s66049 (PMID 25709399): AZD3199 systemic availability lower in COPD than in healthy volunteers or asthma; supports the dose-7 exposure note (optional).
rule_questions: Rule 6 opening year: when the model paper postdates the first trial (AZD3199 trial start 2009 vs Stocks 2014; PF-00610355 trial 2008 vs Glossop 2010; vilanterol dog study FD2008 vs 2013 review), should model_first_use_year use the trial start as the 'proxy allowed', or the first public record as drafted?

Does a pooled model-based (K-PD) analysis of a trial's primary-endpoint data (Nielsen 2012 for NCT00808288) count as the primary-endpoint result for the efficacy cell when the trial itself never reported?

Does a medicinal-chemistry design claim resting on PK (rapid phase II clearance to minimise systemic effects, Glossop 2010) count as a model's stated safety prediction, or must the prediction come from a harm readout in a species?

When the only patient-side safety comparison for a track is in another indication (AZD3199 potassium vs formoterol in asthma) and the context's own trial reports only 'no safety concerns', does imported_from permit same on the COPD track?

For a human_genetic patient-level track (ADRB2 genotype and vilanterol response, Condreay 2016) where no genotype effect was found, is the status contra (the genotype model predicted differential response) or same (the sponsor's null hypothesis held)? The rules do not define the prediction of a pharmacogenetic analysis.
